questions.q: Which declarative automation tools does this lesson say are retired for new development?
questions.explain: Workflow Rules and Process Builder are both retired for new automation; Flow is the current tool.

questions.q: Where can you see every flow already running in an org, regardless of its type?
questions.explain: Every flow, whatever its type, shows up in the Flows list in Setup.

questions.q: Which four categories does Salesforce group new automations into on the New Automation screen?
questions.explain: The New Automation screen groups options into Triggered, Scheduled, Screen, and Autolaunched categories.

questions.q: A Triggered automation, per this lesson's categories, runs because of what?
options: A user clicking a custom button only
A record change or a platform event, without a user on screen
A change to a page layout
questions.explain: Triggered automations are launched by a record change or a platform event and run without user interaction.

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule of thumb, what kind of logic is Flow almost always a good fit for?
options: Only logic that requires writing Apex classes
Only logic that runs once per year
Logic you can describe as "when X happens, do Y, unless Z"
questions.explain: The lesson's rule of thumb is that if the logic fits a "when X happens, do Y, unless Z" pattern, Flow can almost certainly handle it.
